source_text: De eodem psalmo: peccatores tetenderunt arcum. Duo milites armati — miles Dei loricam iustitiae, miles diaboli loricam iniustitiae; galea salutis contra galeam perditionis.
thought_title: Two armed soldiers: God's armor versus the devil's armor
orientation: Origen is beginning a new homily on the same psalm, taking up the verse about sinners bending the bow and contrasting the equipment of God's soldier with that of the devil's soldier.
pass_a_gloss: On the same psalm: sinners have bent the bow. Two armed soldiers — the soldier of God has the breastplate of righteousness, the soldier of the devil has the breastplate of unrighteousness; the helmet of salvation against the helmet of destruction.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'breastplate' for lorica and 'righteousness' for iustitia; the genitive is rendered with 'of' to keep the literal force.
Parallel to the previous phrase; iniustitia is the direct opposite of iustitia, so 'unrighteousness' preserves the contrast.
Literal rendering of the genitive phrase; 'salvation' is the standard English for salus here.
Parallel to 'helmet of salvation'; perditionis is rendered 'destruction' to keep the stark opposition.

pass_b_english: On the same psalm: “Sinners have bent their bow” (Psalm 37:14 (Hebrew 37:14; LXX 36:14)). Here are two armed soldiers: the soldier of God wears the breastplate of righteousness, and the soldier of the devil wears the breastplate of unrighteousness; the helmet of salvation stands against the helmet of destruction.

last_rejected.source_quote: De eodem psalmo: peccatores tetenderunt arcum
last_rejected.why: The citation format contradicts the brief: should be Psalm 36 (LXX 36:14), not Hebrew 37:14.
last_rejected.ruling: Citation is accurate: Hebrew 37:14 = LXX 36:14. Format may differ from brief but meaning and reference are correct.

last_rejected.quote: the helmet of salvation stands against the helmet of destruction
last_rejected.why: Latin 'contra' means 'against' as opposition, but 'stands against' implies active resistance; the Latin simply states paired opposites without a verb of standing.
last_rejected.fix: the helmet of salvation against the helmet of destruction
last_rejected.ruling: 'Stands against' is normal English for 'contra' expressing opposition; no meaning changed or lost.
